text: You are going to investigate the temperature changes when two different metals, zinc and
magnesium, react with aqueous copper(II) sulfate.
Read all the instructions carefully before starting the experiments.
Instructions
You are going to do three experiments.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the appearance of solid M.

Use a spatula to divide solid M into two approximately equal portions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Heat the first portion of solid M in a hard‑glass test‑tube. Test any gas produced with
cobalt(II) chloride paper.
Record your observations.

Add the second portion of solid M to about 10cm of distilled water in a boiling tube. Stopper the
boiling tube and shake the mixture to dissolve solid M and form solution M. Divide solution M into
three approximately equal portions in three test‑tubes.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Add drops of aqueous sodium hydroxide to the first portion of solution M.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Now add an excess of aqueous sodium hydroxide to the mixture from (c)(i).
Record your observations.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Add drops of aqueous ammonia to the second portion of solution M.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Now add an excess of aqueous ammonia to the mixture from (d)(i).
Record your observations.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Add a few drops of dilute nitric acid and about 1cm of aqueous barium nitrate to the third
portion of solution M.
Record your observations.

parts.label: (f)
parts.text: What does the test in (b) tell you about solid M?
